rationale: Same group by name: ACD's Proto-Philippines and Wiktionary's Proto-Philippine; ACD gives no glottocode and Wiktionary's family phi has none.
Same node by name: Central-Eastern Malayo-Polynesian; neither side has a glottocode the catalog links.
Same node by name: Eastern Malayo-Polynesian; the catalog gives pqe-pro only family context for east2712.
Proto-Polynesian is poly1242; the catalog also gives that glottocode to Wiktionary's Eastern Polynesian family (poz-pep), which is narrower.
Same group by name: Chamic; ACD gives no glottocode.
Same name, Proto-Rukai; ACD's glottocode ruka1240 is the Rukai language, and Wiktionary files dru-pro under the family map.
Same group by name: Bungku-Tolaki; ACD gives no glottocode.
Same group by name: Lampungic; ACD's glottocode lamp1241 and Wiktionary's family glottocode lamp1243 differ, so the lookup missed it.
Same group by name: South Sulawesi; ACD gives no glottocode.
Wiktionary has no Proto-Western Malayo-Polynesian code; WMP is a geographic grouping, not a subgroup, in Blust's own usage.
Wiktionary has no Proto-Central Malayo-Polynesian code.
Wiktionary has no Proto-Malayo-Javanic code; its Malayo-Sumbawan (poz-msa) and Malayo-Chamic (poz-mcm) are other groupings.
ACD's 'Formosan' is a level of comparison, not a subgroup; Wiktionary has no code for it.
ACD's Malay is Wilkinson 1959, standard peninsular Malay; Wiktionary's ms holds Malay as its standard is written. The catalog links no glottocode to ms.
ACD's Bikol is Mintz and del Rosario Britanico 1985, the Naga standard, which is Central Bikol; ACD's glottocode biko1240 names the whole Bikol group.
ACD's Bontok is Reid 1976, Guina-ang Bontok, a Central Bontoc variety; ACD's glottocode bont1247 names all Bontok.
ACD's Malagasy is Richardson 1885, Merina, on which standard Malagasy rests; Wiktionary's mg holds standard Malagasy. The catalog links no glottocode to mg.
Same language: Glottolog lamp1243 is Lampung Api, Wiktionary's ljp; the catalog links no glottocode to ljp.
